Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The class's carried-forward build with a floor under it. 3.2.0 halves Counterattack and Counter Swarm damage from 150% to 75% - a direct cut to the only damage source the base build has - and the compensating gift, a new paragon board granting roughly 80% increased damage to storm skills, is a storm board and does nothing for a poison build. The digest's read is that the class comes out net sideways and both aggregator lists hold Spiritborn at A, unchanged. This variant assumes the halving is real and that the compensation is not available, and moves weight off the swarm and onto the skills that are already on the bar and are not mentioned in the patch at all: Ravager, Rushing Claw and Scourge. The swarm stays - it is still the reason to play the archetype - but it stops being the only thing that can kill something. One genuine PTR upside: this is one of the few builds in the repo that can actually take Splinter of Hellfire, because its damage really is damage-over-time dominant and damage over time cannot crit.

Rotation
  1. Ravager to bank Ferocity, Rushing Claw to convert it and move, Counterattack for the swarms, Scourge on anything that is still alive.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Rushing Claw through the pack and let the swarms work, with Scourge and Ravager filling the gap the halving leaves.
Move on when Loyalty's Mantle equipped, or level 70 on the PTR when Mrak hands it to you.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged in shape. The measurement worth taking on the PTR is what share of your damage the swarms still represent after the 150% to 75% cut.
Move on when Harmony of Ebewaka equipped and the swarm share measured.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Ravager to bank Ferocity, Rushing Claw to convert and move, Counterattack for the swarms, Scourge on anything that lives. This is the stage where the Splinter decision gets made on evidence rather than on theory.
Move on when [ptr] A dummy test done on Splinter of Hellfire versus Splinter of Anguish. If your direct-damage floor is large enough that -100% Critical Strike Chance hurts, take Anguish and say so.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested on 3.2.0. Expect the swarm to feel visibly weaker than it did on live and the direct-damage floor to be doing more of the work than this page's stage order implies. Re-verify at launch.

[ptr] No Season 15 filter exists anywhere as of 2026-08-09, so this is the Season 14 in-guide code used as a floor. Check before importing that it is not hiding critical-strike rolls: this variant carries crit further than the build the filter was written for.

Uniques
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Lord Zir, The Darkened Way east of Kyovashad, Fractured Peaks; 1x Lair Key from the Blood Maiden in Helltide. Where →
  • helm [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Bartuc, via Infernal Hordes in Kehjistan near the Yshari Sanctum waypoint; 1x Infernal Hordes Compass, 666 Burning Aether. Forces Jaguar primary and Jaguar secondary because of the class-wide Spirit tag inheritance bug. Where →
  • helm [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Bartuc, same Infernal Hordes route as Loyalty's Mantle. Moves the Spirit Hall pairing to Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary. Carried warning: its granted skill ranks occasionally cause Ravager to lose its 4-rank minimum at 30 ranks, which matters more here because Ravager is part of the direct-damage floor. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Duriel, King of Maggots, The Gaping Crevasse east of Gea Kul, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key. Where →

How to run them

[ptr] Carried over from Season 14 unchanged: 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries and does not mention them. Identical across all eight of the guide's variants, and quoted almost verbatim: hire Subo 'for his map hacks and increased damage from Scorched Earth & Incendiary Bolt', reinforce with Raheir's Bastion 'for additional DR & Unstoppable'. The map visibility is not a luxury on a build whose entire point is crossing a map as fast as possible, and Bastion is doing the survivability work that a build with no defensive skill on the bar cannot do for itself.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The class's carried-forward build with a floor under it. 3.2.0 halves Counterattack and Counter Swarm damage from 150% to 75% - a direct cut to the only damage source the base build has - and the compensating gift, a new paragon board granting roughly 80% increased damage to storm skills, is a storm board and does nothing for a poison build. The digest's read is that the class comes out net sideways and both aggregator lists hold Spiritborn at A, unchanged. This variant assumes the halving is real and that the compensation is not available, and moves weight off the swarm and onto the skills that are already on the bar and are not mentioned in the patch at all: Ravager, Rushing Claw and Scourge. The swarm stays - it is still the reason to play the archetype - but it stops being the only thing that can kill something. One genuine PTR upside: this is one of the few builds in the repo that can actually take Splinter of Hellfire, because its damage really is damage-over-time dominant and damage over time cannot crit.

Rotation
  1. Ravager to bank Ferocity, Rushing Claw to convert it and move, Counterattack for the swarms, Scourge on anything that is still alive.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Rushing Claw through the pack and let the swarms work, with Scourge and Ravager filling the gap the halving leaves.
Move on when Loyalty's Mantle equipped, or level 70 on the PTR when Mrak hands it to you.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged in shape. The measurement worth taking on the PTR is what share of your damage the swarms still represent after the 150% to 75% cut.
Move on when Harmony of Ebewaka equipped and the swarm share measured.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Ravager to bank Ferocity, Rushing Claw to convert and move, Counterattack for the swarms, Scourge on anything that lives. This is the stage where the Splinter decision gets made on evidence rather than on theory.
Move on when [ptr] A dummy test done on Splinter of Hellfire versus Splinter of Anguish. If your direct-damage floor is large enough that -100% Critical Strike Chance hurts, take Anguish and say so.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested on 3.2.0. Expect the swarm to feel visibly weaker than it did on live and the direct-damage floor to be doing more of the work than this page's stage order implies. Re-verify at launch.

Reasoning

Based onEvade Counterswarm Spiritborn
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. [ptr] Rushing Claw takes Evolving Claws rather than staying purely on Evasive Swipe from the late endgame on, so the charge refill feeds a real direct-damage cadence instead of only mobility. The base build already makes this switch at its late stages; here it is the point of the variant rather than a detail.
  2. [ptr] Scourge is ranked and kept ranked at every stage rather than being a one-point Vulnerable application. With the swarm halved, its own damage is a larger share of the total than it was.
  3. [ptr] Critical strike chance is carried further than the base build carries it. The class-wide rule that crit is only there to proc Widow's Web assumes all the damage is the swarm's damage-over-time; a variant with a direct-damage floor breaks that assumption by design.
  4. [ptr] Soul Splinter: Splinter of Hellfire, and this is the rare build where that is defensible. It gives 40-100% increased damage at the cost of -100% Critical Strike Chance, and the digest's own read is that only a non-crit or damage-over-time-dominant build can take it. Verify on a dummy first - if the direct-damage floor this variant adds turns out to be a meaningful share of the total, Hellfire becomes a catastrophic pick and Splinter of Anguish is the answer instead. That tension is real and this page does not hide it.
  5. [ptr] The Swarm of Storms board is deliberately not recorded in this build's paragon layout. It is new in 3.2.0, it is not in the pinned 3.1.0 game database this site draws boards from, and it is a storm board on a poison build. If a Spiritborn skill on this bar turns out to carry the Storm tag, that changes - see spiritborn-theorycraft-swarm-of-storms, which exists to ask exactly that question.
  6. [ptr] No War Plans on either page: 3.2.0 changes nothing about the system and no per-build picks exist for any season.
